P1.evidence: Setter acknowledged but nothing read back — 'You spoke with Kim. He kind of gave me, like, an overview. I feel like I've got a head start.' — and the claimed head start was immediately contradicted: the prospect did not know what the call was, 'I wasn't sure what exactly this was when I first clicked on it.' A genuine read-back would have caught that in the first thirty seconds. Frame was the standard two-part version. Agreement requested and given ('All right. Okay, cool.'), open question ran verbatim.

P2.evidence: No baseline question of any kind. Not age, height, weight, work, training, diet, sleep or energy. Marked as misses rather than not_applicable because the call was live for over five minutes and the rep chose a commitment challenge instead. Three health disclosures arrived unprompted and all three were dropped without a single follow-up: 'I've got bad body aches and pains', 'anxiety and things started kicking in, things that never really affected me before', and 'I got injured, tore my bicep... never really mentally got over it fully.' The bicep injury in particular is the whole reason he stopped, and nobody asked when it happened, whether it healed, or what he can currently do.

P3.evidence: No goals phase at all. The only goal on record was volunteered in his opening answer and never developed: 'just trying to get in a better physical fitness and just kind of sort of get back into shape.' He has twin boys just under two — the strongest available drive-through to family and identity in the batch — and it was mentioned once, as an obstacle, and never revisited as a reason.

P4.evidence: The one phase that partly ran, and it ran on a good question: 'You said you've kind of let yourself go. Tell me about it. What's going on?' That produced the complete history in one answer — twenty years of consistent training, COVID, anxiety, the torn bicep, the twins. Then nothing. No 'why do you feel it didn't stick', no 'what's the one thing actually getting in the way', and no attempt to let him name the gap. He had just handed over four distinct causes and none was examined.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame, and this is the phase the call needed. The prospect's blocker was internal readiness, which is precisely what the consequence frame exists to move — 'if nothing changes, what does life look like over the next two years' asked of a man with twin toddlers, an unrepaired identity as a lifter and two years of drift would have been the entire call. Instead the rep tested commitment directly and, when it came back weak, accepted the answer.

P6.evidence: Neither the belief question nor the all-in question was asked. The rep did apply a readiness gate twice and correctly refused to proceed without a yes: 'if you're not really there yet and you don't, it's like, you don't need to talk about coaching, man. It's fine.' That is half of P6c executed properly. The other half was skipped — the script says that when hesitation surfaces you return to Phase 5, and Phase 5 had never been run in the first place, so there was nothing to return to. He released the prospect instead.

P11.evidence: No close was attempted and no offer was ever presented. Price was never mentioned on this call.

objection_plays.detail: The most clearly applicable play in the batch, and not one move ran. The trigger is unmistakable and repeated: 'I just mentally, I just don't think I'm there quite, quite yet', 'I don't want to be a waste of time', and an injury he 'never really mentally got over'. The burned-before move is written almost exactly for this man — 'if you got hurt in a relationship once, do you never trust again?' maps directly onto someone who tore a bicep and never came back to the gym. Also unused: 'would it be fair to say you're looking for certainty', the pleasure-versus-pain question, the bridge, the plane, and 'how will you know if you never actually try'. The rep's response was 'It's fair, dude. It's fine.'

Explicit think-about-it at 00:04:43. One question was asked — 'Why would you be a waste of time?' — which is not a scripted move and which the prospect deflected without answering. Nothing followed. No 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you there', no 'what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is'. The rep moved to close the call within twenty seconds.

Timing trigger in the prospect's first substantive answer — unpredictable time, twin toddlers, plans that evaporate. The play's core argument is built for exactly this ('things never slow down; when does it actually become the right time') and 'what if all you had to do was show up and everything else was handled' is a direct answer to a man whose stated problem is that he cannot plan. The rep partially addressed the delivery model but never ran the timing argument.

Script gap, and an important one. The prospect disclosed post-COVID anxiety as a cause of his decline. There is no guidance anywhere in the playbook for a prospect whose blocker is a mental health issue rather than a sales objection, and the rep's improvisation converted it into a question of priority and willpower: 'commitment level is the most important thing, right, whenever you want anything in life... if you really want to get back in and that's something that's a high priority, we can help you out. But if it's not, we can't.' What the script needs here is not a better rebuttal but explicit direction on how to acknowledge a disclosure like this and whether to proceed at all.

notes: Six minutes and effectively no process: no baseline, no goals, no consequence frame, and three health disclosures — a torn bicep, chronic aches, and new-onset anxiety — that were heard and dropped. The rep correctly refused to sell into a weak commitment, which is the right instinct, but the script says to return to Phase 5 when hesitation surfaces and Phase 5 had never been run. The coachable point is precise: a prospect saying 'I'm not mentally there yet' is the OE trigger, not the end of the call.
